curation.description: Analyst comparisons between operational experience and the purpose of existing CoreDoc rules. Source answers are embedded in each report; translation is identified explicitly. Contextual corroboration remains pending_validation and does not imply specialist normative approval.

CORE-002.1.statement: Where a financial subject has a lifecycle, it SHALL have one declared current state. Its state SHALL change only through a declared transition from that state after all applicable conditions have passed.
CORE-002.1.title: Lifecycle changes require a declared valid transition

CORE-002.2.statement: A proposed financial change SHALL be evaluated against the complete proposed result and declared relevant facts before it becomes observable. Validation or transition-condition evaluation SHALL NOT itself alter domain data.
CORE-002.2.title: Validation is complete, fact-based, and non-mutating

CORE-002.3.statement: A rejected financial action SHALL leave relevant observable financial state, financial data, and committed history unchanged, unless a governing rule expressly defines another failure effect.
CORE-002.3.title: Rejected actions have no partial financial effect

CORE-003.1.statement: A committed financial event SHALL preserve a stable event identity, declared event type, affected financial subject, and unambiguous occurrence time. It SHALL identify the responsible actor when known.
CORE-003.1.title: A committed event preserves essential evidence

CORE-003.3.statement: A correction, reversal, void, or supersession SHALL preserve a verifiable relationship to the affected original subject or event. It SHALL NOT erase or rewrite original financial facts or history, and these concepts SHALL NOT be silently treated as interchangeable.
CORE-003.3.title: Corrections and related evolution preserve original facts

CORE-004.1.statement: An approval requirement SHALL identify the subject requiring approval, eligible decision-maker or eligibility rule, and the outcome that satisfies or rejects it. Eligibility SHALL be evaluated independently from technical ability to submit a request.
CORE-004.1.title: Approval requirements state subject, eligibility, and outcome

CORE-004.3.statement: An approval decision SHALL identify its requirement, deciding actor, outcome, time, and relevant subject facts or state. It SHALL NOT be assumed valid after relevant facts change, and a committed decision SHALL NOT be overwritten or removed from logical approval history.
CORE-004.3.title: Decisions remain tied to their facts and history

CORE-005.1.statement: A continuing financial subject SHALL have an identifier unique within its declared scope and stable throughout its lifecycle. Distinct subjects SHALL NOT share that identifier within the same scope.
CORE-005.1.title: Continuing financial subjects retain stable identity

CORE-005.3.statement: For the same declared inputs, financial state, and relevant context, a financial evaluation SHALL produce the same observable outcome. A dependency on an external fact SHALL be identified when it affects that outcome.
CORE-005.3.title: Evaluation follows declared facts and context
